title: Jagadish Chandra Bose's birth chart
metaDescription: Jagadish Chandra Bose's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 7.8° Sagittarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The chart's headline is a opposition: Mars and Saturn within 0.4°, drive wired to structure. Across the wheel, each body sees the other in full. The old reading is not conflict so much as permanent mutual visibility.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Measured rather than labelled, the Sun holds 7.8° Sagittarius: the first decan, whose classical sub-ruler is Jupiter. A fire sign, read here in its first face.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: Mercury holds 24.5° Sagittarius, Venus holds 28.7° Sagittarius, Mars holds 12.7° Aquarius — in the old shorthand, a mind that decides at speaking speed; taste that runs toward the vivid and the immediate; drive that argues its way forward.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Mars and Saturn hold the closest angle here — a opposition, 0.4° wide. The scheme reads an opposition as a axis to walk, not a fight to win: the chart keeps both ends lit. Behind it, Mercury square Neptune at 2.4°, and Mercury conjunction Venus at 4.2° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: Mercury opposes Jupiter while both square Neptune. The t-square is the figure the old texts trusted for output: friction with a fixed address. The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Three planets here sit in a sign the classical scheme scores. Mercury in Sagittarius at 24.5° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Jupiter in Gemini at 17.7° is in detriment; Saturn in Leo at 12.3° is in detriment. Condition, not character: that is all the dignity table ever measured.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Of the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: 4 in fire, 4 in air, 1 in water, 1 in earth by element, 6 mutable, 3 fixed, 1 cardinal by modality. Venus, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — the optical reversal the tradition reads as review — energy turned over before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Libra for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 12.9° between midnight and midnight. The sign survives the missing hour; the degree does not, and is given as a reference rather than a fact. At the noon reference it stands at 8.6°.
